Active matter -self-diffusophoresis, squirmer model, fabrication. Biological soft matter – lipid bi-layer membranes, Polymersomes, biopolymers, DNA, proteins.
ME F325.title: Fundamentals of Soft Matter

ME F326.description: Basics of mechanics of materials and fluid mechanics, Destructive and non-destructive testing and characterisation, Centre of percussion, coefficient of restitution, energy absorption, modal analysis; Design of sports equipment, for example, cricket bat, golf club, hockey stick, tennis racquets, cycling, rowing boats and oars, archery, javelin, pole vault etc.; Flow regimes around balls: golf, tennis, football, cricket; Aerodynamics of ball swing, spin and throw; trajectory analysis, spinning effects on ball flight; shuttle cock; Sports surfaces, Ball/surface interaction, Shoe/surface interaction, Sportswear; Biomechanics, stance and body posture, Gait analysis.
ME F326.title: Mechanics of Sports

ME F340.description: The course essentially prepares engineering students to utilize their existing technical knowhow for sports applications. The specific topics will include, working with human and human movement patterns, qualitative and quantitative techniques for analysis of human movement. Sports performance measure and analysis. Anthropomorphy, Ergonomics and Task design. Computer application in sports, computerized performance measure. Sports surface and its impact on sports performance, surface testing methods. Sports and training equipment case study, business around sports.
ME F340.title: Introduction to Sports Engineering

ME F341.description: Theoretical analysis of energy and momentum transfer between fluid and rotor; principles of axial, mixed and radial flow compressors, turbines and pumps; design considerations; cascade aerodynamics and performance limitations; applications to power plant systems; model similitude for turbo-machines; Introduction to fluid power system, laboratory exercises in testing reciprocating machines, rotary machines and fluid power system.
ME F341.title: Prime Movers & Fluid Machines

ME F342.description: CAD software and CAD hardware. Mathematical modeling of parametric curves, surfaces and solids, and their computer simulation on spreadsheets and using specialized solid modeling packages. CAD/CAM data exchange. Introduction to finite element analysis and FEM practice on a specialized CAE package. Rapid prototyping. Students will be required to do several assignments and one CAD project.
ME F342.title: Computer Aided Design

ME F343.description: Small oscillations of linear dynamical systems, free and forced vibrations of single and multi-degree-of-freedom systems, normal modes and orthogonality relations, generalized co-ordinates and Lagrange's equations, matrix formulation, eigenvalue problem and numerical solutions, transient response of one-dimensional systems, approximate energy methods, continuous system, vibration of string, rods, bars and beams. Introduction to control systems.
ME F343.title: Mechanical Vibrations

ME F344.description: Linear programming methods, simplex method, transportation model and its variants, queuing systems, PERT/CPM, Optimal problem formulation, engineering optimization problems, single variable optimization algorithms, multivariable optimization algorithms, constrained optimization algorithms.
ME F344.title: Engineering Optimization

ME F367.description: These courses include projects involving laboratory investigation or laboratory development in the students discipline or interdisciplinary areas. These courses are normally available to students in third or higher levels. These courses must coterminate with project reports.
ME F367.title: Lab Project

ME F377.description: These courses are intended to impart training in design of product/ process or other artifact to the students in the discipline or interdisciplinary areas. These courses are normally available to students in third or higher levels. These courses must coterminate with project reports.
ME F377.title: Design Project

ME F411.description: Introduction to Fluid power, advantages of fluid power, applications, Introduction to Pneumatics, Air preparation and Components, Pneumatics Circuits and Applications, Electro pneumatics, Electrical Controls for fluid power circuits, , Physical properties of hydraulic fluids, Energy and Power in Hydraulic Systems, Frictional Losses in Hydraulic Pipelines, Hydraulic Pumps, Hydraulic Cylinders and Cushioning Devices, Hydraulic Motors, Hydraulic Valves, Hydraulic Circuit Design and Analysis, Ancillary Hydraulic Devices, Hydraulic Conductions and Fittings, Maintenance of Hydraulic Systems, Use of PLC programming for interfacing pneumatics and Hydraulic Circuits.
ME F411.title: Fluid Power Systems

ME F412.description: Generalized model of production systems; types of production flows; life cycle concepts; facilities location and layout planning; aggregate and batch production planning; inventory systems; materials requirements planning; elements of monitoring & production control.
ME F412.title: Production Planning and Control

ME F413.description: Introduction, sources of nonlinearity, examples, qualitative analysis: phase plane, singular points, stability of singular points, Forced response, Perturbation methods: straightforward expansion, the method of multiple scales, harmonic balance, method of averaging, Nonlinear normal modes, Nonlinear Multiple-DOF Systems, Bifurcations, Centre manifold reduction, Flouquet Theory, Chaos Theory, Melnikov Criterion, Applications to vehicle dynamics, structures and microsystems etc. Use of softwares for simulations and numerical solutions.
ME F413.title: Nonlinear Vibrations

ME F414.description: Introduction to fuel cell, types, advantages and applications;Fuel cell thermodynamics, electrochemistry, chargetransport, heat and mass transport; Fuel cell modelling andsimulation. In-situ, ex-situ experimental characterizationtechniques viz. polarization curve, electrochemicalimpedance spectroscopy, current density mapping etc.Polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cell including directliquid fuel cell; Other fuel cells viz. SOFC, AFC, MCFC,PAFC, biological fuel cells etc. and recent development.
ME F414.title: Fuel Cell Science and Technology

ME F415.description: Introduction to Gas Dynamics, Basic equations of compressible flow, Wave propagation, Steady one-dimensional flow (Varyingarea adiabatic flow), Normal shock waves, Oblique shock and expansion waves, Prandtl-Meyer Flow, Flow with Friction and Heat Transfer, Potential equation for compressible flow, Similarity rule.
ME F415.title: Gas Dynamics

ME F416.description: Introduction to reverse engineering, methodologies and techniques for reverse engineering, reverse engineering hardware and software, selecting reverse engineering system, introduction to rapid prototyping, relationship between reverse engineering and rapid prototyping. Reverse engineering in automotive engineering, aerospace engineering, medical device industry. Legal aspects and barriers for reverse engineering. Project work.
ME F416.title: Reverse Engineering and Rapid Prototyping

ME F417.description: The stress and strain tensors in macroscopic plasticity and failure criteria for metal forming, effective stress and effective strain, flow rules for plastic deformation and principle of normality. Work hardening, determination of work hardening exponent. Plastic instability and effect of inhomogeneity on uniform strain. Strain rate and temperature effects on plastic deformation and flow stress, superplasticity, temperature rise during metal forming. Ideal work and redundant work. Slab, upper-bound, slip-line field and finite element methods of analysis of various bulk and sheet metal forming processes. Bulk and sheet metal formability tests and forming limit diagram. Sheet metal properties and plastic anisotropy.
ME F417.title: Advanced Metal Forming

ME F418.description: Thrust and specific impulse. Compressible flows. Detailed analysis of liquid, solid and hybrid propulsion systems. Includes propellants, injection systems, combustion and chemical equilibrium, thrust chambers, nozzles and plumes. Electro-thermal thrusters. Plasmas and electromagnetic thrusters.
ME F418.title: Rocket and Spacecraft Propulsion

ME F419.description: Quality design across global supply chain. Robust product architecture for market variety and technology advances. Product development risk management.
ME F419.title: Total Product Integration Engineering

ME F420.description: Classification of power plants. Components and layout of; thermal, nuclear, hydro electric power plants. Site selection for various power plants. Combined cycle power plants. Magneto Hydro Dynamics (MHD) systems. Economics of power generation, economic loading of power stations. Load curve analysis; load factor, diversity factor. Power plant instrumentation and controls.
ME F420.title: Power Plant Engineering

ME F423.description: Introduction to microfluidics, scaling in microfluidics, theoretical microfluidics, Philosophy of Computational Fluid Dynamics, Concepts of discretization, fabrication techniques for microfluidic devices, microvalves, micropumps, microflow sensors, microfluidics for life sciences: micromixers, microneedles, microfilters, microseparators, microreactors, modeling and simulation on CAD tool.
ME F423.title: Micro Fluidics and its Application

ME F424.description: World and Indian energy scenario; energy policy;energy management principles; energy conservation;energy auditing; analysis; formulation of energymanagement options; economic evaluation,implementation & control; energy conservationtechniques – conservation in energy intensiveindustries; choice of fuels and stoichiometry, steamgeneration, distribution systems, and electricalsystems; integrated resource planning; demand-sidemanagement; cogeneration; total energy schemes;thermal insulation; energy storage; economicevaluation of conservation technologies; analysis oftypical applications.
ME F424.title: Energy Management

ME F425.description: Introduction to Additive Manufacturing (AM), generalized AM process and process chain, differentmaterials used in AM, Use of multiple materials, multifunctional and graded materials in AM, Role ofsolidification rate. Various AM processes and theirmechanics of operation. Vat polymerization processes, stereolithography. Powder based AM processesinvolving sintering and melting, selective lasersintering, direct metal laser sintering, selective lasermelting, other polymer, ceramic, metal and alloyK-4powder based AM processes. Extrusion based AMprocesses, fused deposition modelling (FDM). Sheetlamination processes, laminated object manufacturing(LOM). Microand nano‐additive manufacturingprocesses; Modelling in Additive ManufacturingTransport phenomena models: temperature and fluidflow, molten pool formation, Various case studies ‐modelling of fusion based AM process, powder bedmelting based process, droplet based printing process;Applications of Additive Manufacturing in Aerospace,Automotive, Electronics industries and Biomedicalapplications.
ME F425.title: Additive Manufacturing

ME F426.description: Limitations of existing manufacturing systems, industrial revolution 4.0 for manufacturing, vision andstrategy, organization and structure, models andstandards, drivers and enablers, smart products, smartprocess, smart production, smart factories, smartnetworked industries, smart supply chain, lean andI4.0. I4.0 navigators: sensors, actuators, data analytics, connectivity, and AI. Economic evaluation of existingsystem for I4.0. Limitations of I4.0. Case studies.
ME F426.title: Industry 4.0 in Manufacturing

ME F427.description: Introduction to tensors, tensor algebra and tensor calculus. Kinematics of deformation (displacement, velocity, deformation gradient, material and spatial field descriptions, description of local deformation, linearized kinematics, kinematic rates), left & right Cauchy-Green deformation tensor, Cauchy-Lagrangian strain tensor. Traction and stress (first Piola-Kirchhoff stress, second Piola- Kirchhoff stress, Biot stress etc). Mechanical conservation and balance laws (conservation of mass, conservation of linear momentum, conservation of angular momentum, conservation of energy, work done by stresses and the principle of virtual work, BVP, IVP, calculus of variation). Constitutive relations (constraints on constitutive relations, frame indifference, objectivity, material symmetry, constitutive models for linearly elastic, hyperelastic solids and fluid flows).
ME F427.title: Continuum Mechanics

ME F428.description: Overview of smart materials. Piezoelectric materials (Ceramics and polymers), Electro and Magneto-Rheological Fluids, Shape Memory Alloys (SMA) – One way and two-way SMAs, Magnetic Shape Memory Alloys (M-SMA), Fiber optic sensors, Miscellaneous smart materials – Magnetostrictive, electrostrictive materials and others. Basic modelling of smart materials, Dynamics and control knowledge for smart materials. Applications in the field of civil, mechanical, aerospace, biomedical, energy industry such as sensors and actuators, vibration control and damping, structural health monitoring. Intelligent devices based on smart materials. Pre-requisites: ME F216 or MF F216 or CHE F243

prerequisite.text: ME F216 or MF F216 or CHE F243

ME F428.title: Smart Materials

ME F429.description: Introduction to energy carriers at micro/nanoscale, energy levels at micro/nanoscale, energy transport by waves and particles, energy quantization, energy states in solids, scattering and heat generation processes, statistical thermodynamics, micro/nanoscale heat transport: Phonon specific heat, thermal conductance, thermal conductivity, convection and radiation, entropy of energy states. Classical laws, Boltzmann transport equation, deviation from classical laws at micro/nanoscale, phonon-phonon transport, electron-phonon transport. Applications of micro/nanoscale heat transport: micro heat exchanger, micro heat pipes, thermoelectric devices, microchannel heat sinks, microelectronics, nanomaterials, nanoencapsulated heat storage materials, nanofluids, nanoscale thin films and nanosensors. Pre-requisites: ME F220 OR CHE F241

prerequisite.text: ME F220 OR CHE F241

ME F429.title: Micro-Nanoscale Heat Transport

ME F430.description: Introduction to Fluid-Structure Interaction with examples of FSI systems, Coupling fluid and structural mechanics, Coupled fluidstructure equations; Small reduced velocities, Added stiffness and added mass, Computing added mass; Added damping, Sloshing, Coupling with sloshing; Introduction to Aeroelasticity, Flow-induced static instability, Flow-induced dynamic instability, Coupled-mode flutter; Fluid forces on a bluff body with non-circular cross-section, Fluid-induced instabilities, Galloping; Garden hose instability, Fluid-conveying pendulum, Fluidconveying pipes, Vortex-induced vibrations, Vortex-shedding patterns, Lock-in, Wakeinduced flutter; Numerical simulation and modelling of FSI, Coupling fluid and structure codes; Monolithic and partitioned methods for FSI, Spatial and temporal coupling methods at fluidstructure interface. Case studies on: Flutter of an aerofoil, Galloping of a square cylinder, Fluid-elastic instability of offshore risers and cylinder arrays. Pre-requisites: ME F211: Mechanics of Solids, ME F212: Fluid Mechanics

prerequisite.text: ME F211: Mechanics of Solids, ME F212: Fluid Mechanics

ME F430.title: Fluid-Structure Interactions

ME F432.description: Introduction, features of NC machine tools, NC part programming, CAM system devices, interpolators for manufacturing systems, control loops of NC systems, computerized numerical control, adaptive control systems, CAD to CAM, CAPP, industrial robots, computer aided production planning & control, computer aided inspection and quality control, CIM systems.
ME F432.title: Computer Aided Manufacturing

ME F433.description: Fundamentals of solar energy and radiation: earth–sun angles, solar spectrum, radiation geometry, and measurement techniques. Estimation of solar energy on horizontal and tilted surfaces. Solar energy conversion technologies: flat plate collectors, concentrating collectors, geometric optics, and tracking systems. Heat transfer analysis: conduction, convection, radiation, and thermal modeling of components. Thermal energy storage systems and materials. Performance equations, system simulation, and load matching for timedependent energy demands. Applications in solar water heating, space heating and cooling, industrial process heat, and solar refrigeration. Life cycle cost analysis and techno-economic evaluation. Use of simulation tools for system design and performance analysis. Laboratory and project components include testing, modeling, and analysis of solar thermal systems. Policy and regulatory aspects.
ME F433.title: Solar Thermal Process Engineering

ME F434.description: Digital Twins for condition monitoring and prognostics - Digital Twins for prognostics, fault diagnosis in rotating machines, electrical machinery faults, thermography, computer vision technique for wear debris analysis, acoustic analysis, Mathematical modelling and physics-based approach, communication protocols between physical and virtual systems, data-driven or AI/MLbased approach for digital twins, and hybrid approach. Digital twins in Manufacturingoperations improvement, tool condition monitoring, 3-D printing. Digital Twins in Aerospace systems and automobiles.
ME F434.title: Digital Twins in Mechanical Engineering

ME F435.description: Introduction to Shape Memory Alloys (SMA), Mechanism of shape memory effect and superelasticity, Ti-Ni, Cu, Fe – based SMAs, Magnetic SMA, Fabrication and experimental characterization of SMA, SMA Constitutive Modelling, Design and applications of SMA components in aerospace, biomedical and structural engineering, Experiments on shape memory effect, superelasticity, shape setting, spring design and fabrication, SMA component design, fabrication and demonstration for various applications.
ME F435.title: Shape Memory Alloys: Fundamentals and Applications

ME F436.description: Introduction, necessity of sustainable energy technologies, classification, principles, challenges, comparison and applications of different sustainable energy technologies. Basics of decarbonization, decentralization and digitalization of energy systems. Energy informatics: Internet of energy, energy blockchain, artificial intelligence tools and machine learning techniques used for energy data analytics, energy forecasting, optimization and management of next generation sustainable energy systems.
ME F436.title: Sustainable Energy Informatics

ME F437.description: Review of basics of thermodynamics and fluid mechanics in the context of food engineering, thermo-physical properties of foods, energy and controls in food processing, heat transfer in food processing, preservation processes, refrigeration and freezing aspects of foods, evaporation processes in food processing, Dehydration processes of foods, design and analysis of equipment for all the above processes, case studies of these as applied to different kinds of foods.
ME F437.title: Thermo-fluidic of Food Process Engineering

ME F438.description: Technology World of micro and Nano, Moore’s Law, Cleanroom for device fabrication, Introduction of lithography process, Physical and Chemical Modes of Crystal Growth, Piezoelectric Materials, Mechanical and Electrical Modeling, Performance Summary of Piezoelectric Microcantilevers for Vibration Energy Harvesting, Development of Triboelectric Energy Harvesters, Acoustic Micro harvester, Electrostatic Conversion Method, Design Consideration and Optimization, Pyroelectric Energy Harvesting, Introduction to Photovoltaic Physics, Optical Properties of Nanostructures; Bio-MEMS Applications, Tire Pressure Monitoring in Automobiles, Structural Health Monitoring, Sustainable Electronics, Case Study of Energy-Harvesting Electronics, Interface Electronics for Piezoelectric Energy Harvesting, Interface Electronics for Electromagnetic Energy Harvesting. World of micro and nano, Moore’s Law, Device fabrication, Introduction of lithography process, Physical and Chemical Modes of Crystal Growth, Piezoelectric Materials - Mechanical and Electrical Modelling, Performance Summary of Piezoelectric Microcantilevers for Vibration Energy Harvesting, Development of Triboelectric Energy Harvesters, Acoustic Micro harvester, Magneto thermoelectric devices, Pyroelectric Energy Harvesting, Photovoltaic Devices; Bio-MEMS Applications, Tire Pressure Monitoring in Automobiles, Structural Health Monitoring, Sustainable Electronics, Case Study of Energy-Harvesting Electronics. Piezoelectric Devices and Materials, Piezoelectric Microcantilevers for Energy Harvesting, Triboelectric Energy Harvesters, Acoustic Micro-energy harvester, Thermoelectric Devices and Materials, Magneto thermoelectric devices, Pyroelectric Energy Harvesting, Photovoltaic Devices; Bio-MEMS, Case studies on piezoelectric/photovoltaic /thermoelectric/Triboelectric applications, Simulation techniques.
ME F438.title: Micro and Nano Energy Harvesting

ME F439.description: History, hardware and software components, subsystems, drag and lift, basic aerodynamic equations, propulsion systems, longitudinal, lateral and dynamic stability, pitch and lateral controls, static and dynamic loads, application types and payloads, mission planning, navigation and modes of control, data links, launch and recovery systems, regulatory policies, safety, technical challenges and recent advances.
ME F439.title: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle

ME F441.description: Internal combustion engines; vehicle performance; analysis and design of vehicle components. Experimental or theoretical investigation of problems selected from the field of automotive vehicles.
ME F441.title: Automotive Vehicles

ME F443.description: Basic concepts of probability and probability distributions, standard probability distribution, sampling and sampling distributions, confidence intervals, testing significance, statistical tolerance, various types of control charts, statistical process control techniques, value analysis, defect diagnosis and prevention, basic concepts of reliability, reliability design evaluation and control, methods of applying total quality management, production process. ME F451 Mechanical Equipment Design Design analysis for additional machine elements; retainment of bearings and design of machine housing; introduction to techniques of optimisation reliability and value analysis; exercises in detail design; design solutions to meet specified functional requirements.
ME F443.title: Quality Control, Assurance and Reliability

ME F452.description: Introduction to composites, concepts of reinforcement, strengthening mechanisms, fibrous reinforcements, matrix materials, micro-mechanical aspects of composites, manufacturing methods, composite production design methods-design of tensile members, pressure vessels, storage tanks, and other chemical process equipment made of FRP, design of joints, damage of composites by impact, FRP grids, recent development in manufacturing of composites and technologies.
ME F452.title: Composite Materials & Design

ME F461.description: Principles, thermodynamic analysis, load estimates and design of various refrigeration and air conditioning systems for comfort and industrial applications. Theoretical or experimental investigation of refrigeration and air-conditioning problems.
ME F461.title: Refrigeration and Air conditioning

ME F472.description: Concept of accuracy, accuracy of numerical control systems, tolerances and fits, acceptance tests for machine tools, static stiffness and its influence on machining accuracy, inaccuracies due to thermal effects, influence of forced vibrations on accuracy, dimensional wear of cutting tools and its influences on accuracy, clamping and setting errors, location principles and errors due to location, surface roughness and microfinishing processes, dimensioning and dimensional chains, methods of improving accuracy and surface finish, thread and gear measuring instruments, coordinate measuring machines, introduction to computer aided tolerancing.
ME F472.title: Precision Engineering

ME F481.description: Course Description is to be developed.
ME F481.title: Project Appraisal

ME F482.description: Introduction to Combustion, Concepts and Applications, Fuels and Oxidizers, Combustion and Thermochemistry, Chemical Kinetics and Mechanisms, Chain Reactions, Physics of Combustion, Conservation Equations for Reacting Flows, Laminar and Turbulent Premixed Flames, Diffusion Flames, Droplet and Particle Combustion, Emissions.
ME F482.title: Combustion

ME F483.description: Historic development of wind energy technology, basic principles of wind energy conversion, different types of wind machines and their performances, wind rotor aerodynamics and its application in the turbine design, statistical methods of measurement and analysis of wind spectra for energy use, developing models for estimating the wind energy potential of a prospective site, Constructional features of various systems and sub-systems of a Wind Energy Conversion System(WECS), Features of wind farms, performance models of WECS, Optimal matching of WECS, environmental aspects of wind energy conversion, Economics of wind energy conversion.
ME F483.title: Wind Energy

ME F484.description: Automotive vehicle: layout, operating systems, components, materials and production processes; Power unit: IC engine, working principles, performance, systems and the associated parts; Mechanical unit: transmission, drive train, steering, chassis, suspension, brakes, wheels and tyres; Electric unit: battery, charging, starter and lighting; Electronic control unit: application of electronics and computers, sensors, actuators and on-board diagnostics; Latest Trends: advanced combustion systems and hybrid/fuelcell/electrical power systems, alternate fuels and the emissions.
ME F484.title: Automotive Technology

ME F485.description: Introduction to CFD, Partial Differential Equation (PDE): Physical classifications, Mathematical Classifications, Well posed problem. Basic of Discretization Methods: Finite difference method, Truncation error, consistency, error and stability analysis, convergence, various discretization schemes. Introduction commercial software: OpenFOAM or Fluent. Application of numerical methods to selected model equations: Wave equation, Heat equation, Laplace's equations. Solution of Navier-Stokes equation for incompressible flows.
ME F485.title: Numerical Techniques for Fluid Flow and Heat Transfer

ME F491.description: This is an unstructured open-ended course where under the overall supervision of an instructor-in-charge, batches of students will be attached to different instructors. Each batch will work on a specific time-bound project which is of basic or peripheral concern of his discipline. Each student must submit a project report as a culmination of his endeavour and investigation. The instructorincharge will determine the choice of the project and also whether or not the project report is to be submitted jointly by a group or individually by a student. The course will aim to evaluate student's actual ability to use the fundamentals of knowledge and to meet new unknown situations as demonstrated by the students' interaction with the instructors and instructor-incharge and aggregated in the project report. The instructor-incharge may assign specific hours for formal brain-storming sessions.
ME F491.title: Special Project

ME G511.description: Classification of robots & manipulators; fields of application; synthesis of planar & spatial mechanisms; methods of function & path generation; coupler curve synthesis; linkages with open loop; actuators & drive elements; microprocessor application and control of robots.
ME G511.title: Mechanisms & Robotics

ME G512.description: Fundamental concepts, matrix algebra and gaussian limination, one-dimensional problems, trusses, two-dimensional problems using constant strain triangles, axisymmetric solids subjected to axisymmetric loading, two-dimensional isoparametric elements and numerical integration, beams and frames, three-dimensional problems in stress analysis, scalar field problems, dynamic considerations, pre-processing and post processing.
ME G512.title: Finite Element Methods

ME G513.description: Fundamentals of HVAC system design and thermal comfort. Climatic conditions and their influence on building performance. Heat transmission through building envelopes, infiltration, and ventilation effects. Estimation of heating and cooling loads, internal heat gains, and solar effects. HVAC psychrometrics and use of charts for process design. Codes and standards for HVAC system sizing, installation, and performance. Human comfort, indoor air quality, and thermal environment analysis. Air distribution systems: duct design, fan selection, acoustics, and vibration control. Central and zonal air systems, heating and cooling coils, air cleaning, and filtration techniques. Introduction to electrical systems relevant to HVAC operations. Controls and automation for air distribution systems. Laboratory and simulation modules on load calculations, psychrometric processes, and HVAC performance analysis.
ME G513.title: Heating and Cooling of Buildings

ME G514.description: Introduction, thermodynamics, gas turbine plants, steam turbine plants, fluid dynamics, dimensional analysis and performance parameters, flow through cascades, axial turbine stages, high temperature turbine stages, axial compressor stages, centrifugal compressor stages, radial turbine stages, axial fans and propellers, centrifugal fans and blowers, and wind turbines.
ME G514.title: Turbomachinery

ME G515.description: Introduction to CFD and its role in thermal-fluid system design. Governing equations: continuity, momentum, energy; steady/unsteady, compressible/incompressible flows. PDE classification: elliptic, parabolic, hyperbolic; boundary/initial conditions. Discretization: finite difference/volume methods; stability and convergence. Grid generation: structured/unstructured, mesh quality, transformations. Solvers: SIMPLE, PISO; turbulence models: k– ε, k–ω; wall functions. Case studies: Couette flow, nozzles, boundary layers HVAC, and jet impingement. Lab and proficiency component: CFD tools (Fluent, SimScale, OpenFOAM) for simulations. Pre-processing, solver setup, postprocessing using Paraview, Fluent, MATLAB. Python implementation of CFD solvers and convergence studies. Validation against analytical/empirical data. Emphasis on reporting, accuracy, and industrial applications.
ME G515.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics

ME G516.description: Basic concepts of energy conversion, generation of electrical and thermal energy, transmission and distribution of electrical energy, load management, detailed analysis of utilization of thermal energy in : boilers, furnaces, compressors, heat transfer equipments, and HVAC systems, energy audit, waste heat recovery systems, cogeneration, demand side management, and management and organization of energy saving projects.
ME G516.title: Energy Systems Engineering

ME G517.description: Advanced linear algebra and vector calculus: vector spaces, eigenvalues, orthogonality, and tensor notation. ODEs and PDEs: higher-order systems, Sturm–Liouville problems, and applications in dynamics and heat flow. Transform methods: Laplace, Fourier, conformal mapping, and complex variables. Numerical methods: finite difference and finite element approaches, error estimation, convergence analysis. Symbolic computation with SymPy, Maple, or Mathematica. Optimization: linear and nonlinear programming, Euler–Lagrange, Hamilton’s principle. Probability and statistics: distributions, regression, hypothesis testing, reliability analysis Lab and proficiency component: Numerical solutions and visualization using state-of-the art software tools. FEM and FVM simulations for conduction and flow. Optimization of design problems. Transient modeling of HVAC/battery systems. Intro to machine learning for sensor data and fault detection.
ME G517.title: Applied Mathematics

ME G518.description: Energy Systems Thermodynamics and fluid flow fundamentals relevant to renewable energy systems. Energy conversion in solar thermal, wind, hydro, geothermal, ocean, and biomass systems. Thermodynamic and exergy modeling of stand-alone sustainable energy systems and hybrid systems with reheat, regeneration, intercooling, and thermal storage. 4E (energy, exergy, environment, economics) analysis for performance evaluation, environmental impact, and cost-effectiveness. System-level optimization using analytical, numerical, and software tools. Integration of low-carbon technologies into existing energy infrastructures. Lab and proficiency component: Experiments on heat exchangers, solar thermal systems, wind tunnel testing, and CFD-based simulations. Project-based learning for modeling, analysis, and optimization of real-world sustainable energy systems using experimental and computational tools.
ME G518.title: Advanced Thermodynamics for Sustainable

ME G519.description: Fundamentals of fluid dynamics: continuity, Navier–Stokes, vorticity transport, nondepersonalization. Exact solutions: Couette, Poiseuille, unsteady flow, Stokes, lubrication theory. Boundary layers: Blasius, Kármán- Pohlhausen, momentum thickness, flow separation. Turbulence: transition, RANS, Reynolds stress, mixing length, velocity profiles. Internal/external flows: friction factors, Moody diagram, entrance effects. Compressible flow: Mach number, shocks, expansion waves, boundary layer interaction. Special topics: flow instability, non-Newtonian and free surface flows, biofluids. Lab and proficiency component: Use of stateof-the Art/Commercial software for simulations of laminar and vortex shedding flows; vorticity, streamlines, drag/lift estimation. Design based empirical calculations of drag and losses. Comparison of simulation, analytical, and empirical results. Industry relevance: aerospace, hydraulics, R&D.
ME G519.title: Advanced Fluid Dynamics

ME G521.description: Concept of system design; modeling of structural and kinematic systems, and determination of system characteristics; reliability of systems; design of machine elements for specified reliability; concepts of optimization; techniques of design optimization for linear and non-linear problems.
ME G521.title: Mechanical System Design

ME G532.description: Design principles of machine tools; stiffness and rigidity of separate construction elements and their combined behaviour under load; design of stepped and stepless drives; electrical, mechanical and hydraulic drives; design of bearings and sideways; machine tool controls; machine tool dynamics; recent developments in machine tool design.
ME G532.title: Machine Tool Engineering

ME G533.description: Multidimensional and transient conduction with variable properties and phase change. Numerical methods: Crank–Nicolson, ADI, finite volume schemes for complex domains. Thermal contact resistance and interface tracking in composite systems. Radiative exchange in enclosures using view factor matrices and gray surface models. Participating media radiation: RTE, P-1 and DO methods, spectral dependencies. Flame and gas radiation using Hottel’s models; radiation shielding design. Coupled conduction–radiation in multilayered and high-temperature environments. Applications: furnaces, solar receivers, re-entry systems, thermal protection. Lab and proficiency component: Simulation using COMSOL/Fluent; IR-based experimental analysis. MATLAB/Python modeling of conduction–radiation networks.
ME G533.title: Conduction and Radiation Heat Transfer

ME G534.description: Advanced internal/external convection: Graetz, Wiezbicki problems, and entrance effects. Integral methods and similarity-based solutions for complex geometries. Turbulent modeling: Reynolds stress, k–ε, k–ω, and energy dissipation mechanisms. Boiling and condensation: bubble dynamics, flow regimes, critical heat flux models. Mass transfer with heat: Chilton–Colburn analogy, film/penetration models. Coupled heat and mass transfer in evaporation, humidification, absorption systems. High-speed and compressible convection with property variations. Design of compact exchangers, condensers, and phase change systems. Lab and proficiency component: CFD simulation of multi-mode transport using Fluent/COMSOL. Heat/mass transfer modeling in MATLAB/Python; experimental validation.
ME G534.title: Convective Heat and Mass Transfer

ME G535.description: Boundary value problems; wave equations; nonlinear partial differential equations; calculus of variations; Eigen value problems; iteration problems including forward and inverse iteration schemes – Graham Schmidt deflation – simultaneous iteration method – subspace iteration – Lanczo’s algorithm – estimation of core and time requirements.
ME G535.title: Advanced Engineering Mathematics

ME G536.description: Principles of design and analysis of thermal systems and equipment. Heat exchangers: classification, design methodologies, and performance evaluation. Boilers and condensers: thermal sizing, pressure vessel considerations, and efficiency enhancement. Design of cooling towers, evaporators, and thermal storage systems. Combustion chamber design for thermal efficiency and emission control. Material selection for thermal stresses, corrosion, and high-temperature performance. Design codes and standards for thermal equipment. Heat transfer augmentation techniques and compact heat exchanger configurations. Integration of thermal equipment in power plants, refrigeration systems, and renewable energy systems. Simulation and modeling of thermal equipment for steady and transient performance. Laboratory and project components involve thermal design calculations, performance evaluation, and case studies on industrial thermal systems.
ME G536.title: Thermal Equipment Design

ME G537.description: Introduction to cryogenics and its applications, properties of cryogenic fluids, properties of materials at cryogenic temperature, gas-Liquefaction and refrigeration systems, gas separation, cryocoolers, cryogenic insulations, vacuum technology, instrumentation in cryogenics, safety in cryogenics.
ME G537.title: Cryogenic Engineering

ME G538.description: Birth of Toyota production system, house of Toyota production system, stability, standardization, just-in-time,jidoka, involvement, hoshin planning, Toyota culture, Toyota way, Case Studies.
ME G538.title: Toyota Production System

ME G539.description: Computer Modeling for mass property analysis. Computer Numerical Control. Computer-aided Manufacturing, operation of CNC machine tools. Design of manufacturing work cells, Automated Manufacturing and Programmable Controller.
ME G539.title: Computer Integrated Manufacturing

ME G542.description: A detailed overview of Friction welding, Explosive welding, ultrasonic welding, and hybrid welding process; working principle and applications; Heat distribution, metal flow in a liquid and semisolid state; alloying element segregation, macro and microstructure in different weld zones; Selection of welding characteristics for underwater, extreme hot or cold, and in space conditions; Thermal modeling and simulations; governing transport phenomena equations, boundary conditions for individual welding processes; Estimation of the cooling rate, G/R ratio, and grain growth in weld zones.
ME G542.title: Advanced welding techniques

ME G543.description: History of natural refrigerants, Growth in HVACR sector and energy consumption, Impact of refrigerants on environment. Thermodynamic properties of natural refrigerants (Ammonia, Carbon dioxide, Hydrocarbons, Water, Air), Challenges and opportunities of Natural refrigerants, Thermodynamic modelling of various natural refrigeration system. Low charge ammonia system, Transcritical CO2 system, high ambient application, chiller application, deep freezing application, natural refrigerant in secondary loop, Multi stage compression, Booster system, Cascade and multi evaporator system, simultaneous heatingcooling, high temperature heat pump. Technologies for performance enhancement & safety assurance. Component selection and design: Gas cooler, Internal heat exchanger, Sub cooler, Work recovery expander, Ejector, Economizer, Pressure exchanger, Defrost system, Oil management system, Accumulator, Electronic expansion valve, Variable speed drive, Compressors. Waste heat recovery and heat integration,Techno-economics of natural fluids.
ME G543.title: Natural Refrigerants and Application

ME G544.description: Floating frame of reference, Matrix form of dynamic equations of rigid body, Single-input Single-output system, Multiple input Multiple output systems, Fully actuated, Underactuated & Kinematically redundant mechanisms, Zero dynamics, Discontinuous dynamical systems, Hybrid systems, Hybrid control design, Applications - Robot gait kinematics and dynamics, space robotics, vehicle dynamics.
ME G544.title: Multibody Dynamics

ME G545.description: Introduction to neural networks, approximation properties, backpropagation, deep network training, regularization and optimization, convolution neural networks, recurrent neural networks, attention models, transformers, neural architecture search, federated learning, meta-learning, applications in time series modeling and forecasting, online (incremental) learning. *Course description is same as AIML ZG511.
ME G545.title: Deep Neural Networks

ME G546.description: Introduction to neural networks, approximation properties, backpropagation, deep network training, regularization and optimization, convolution neural networks, recurrent neural networks, attention models, transformers, neural architecture search, federated learning, meta-learning, applications in time series modeling and forecasting, online (incremental) learning. *Course description is same as AIML ZG511.
ME G546.title: Advanced Driver Assistance System

ME G547.description: This course explores the concept of Connected Factories and Connected Workforce, focusing on the importance of digitization and the implementation of IoT, AI/ML, AR/VR, robots and cobots, and digital twin technology in manufacturing. Students will examine real-world case studies from industry leaders like General Motors, Siemens, and Tesla, while also addressing business challenges, network security, and data analytics in connected environments. Additionally, the course delves into the role of remote work, digital collaboration, and wearable technology in enhancing employee experience and skills development. *Course description is same as PDSM ZG515.
ME G547.title: Connected Manufacturing

ME G611.description: The course aims at developing complete self reliance in solving analysis & design problems of engineering with the aid of computers. It stresses upon the use of more powerful tools including system planning, simulation and modelling. The student will take up a design project and will work independently on the project guided by the instructor or resource person as and when required. The effort must culminate with a CAAD program and a project report.
ME G611.title: Computer Aided Analysis and Design

ME G612.description: General properties of Plastics, Mechanical Behavior of Plastics, Processing of Plastics like Extrusion, injection moulding, thermoforming, calendaring, rotational moulding, compression moulding, transfer moulding, analysis of polymer melt flow, rheological models for polymer melt flow, analysis of heat transfer during polymer processing, elastic behavior of polymer melts, testing methods of polymers like DSC, TGA, DMA, XRD etc. FRP composites, Properties of FRP composites in longitudinal and transverse directions, volume and weight fraction relationships of fibers, failure mechanisms, mechanical properties and fiber orientation effects, processing of composite materials, advancement of composite materials in applications like wind mill blades, bullet proof jackets, etc.
ME G612.title: Plastics Engineering

ME G613.description: Linear bending, modal and stability analysis of structures; incremental-iterative solution methods for nonlinear static and dynamic problems; nonlinear analysis considering geometric nonlinearity; elastoplastic analysis; alternative numerical approaches; industrial case studies on thermal analysis, coupled field analysis; fluid flow analysis; fatigue, creep and fracture, crash analysis, composite structures, shape optimization Pre-requisite: CE F435 OR CE G619 OR ME G512

prerequisite.text: CE F435 OR CE G619 OR ME G512

ME G613.title: Advanced Finite Element Modelling & Analysis

ME G614.description: Topology optimization by the distribution of isotropic material, minimum compliance design problem formulation, solid isotropic material with penalization (SIMP) technique, and other solution methods. Combining topology and shape design, incorporating multiple load types and variable thickness. Topology optimization of dynamic problems involving free and forced vibrations and buckling, compliant mechanisms, multiphysics problems, multimaterial structures, material design problems, and wave propagation problems. Topology optimization of anisotropic material structures, homogenization formulas for layered and composite structures. Topology optimization of truss structures, minimum compliance truss design, contact mechanics problems. Computational procedures and examples on numerical analysis and finite element analysis packages.
ME G614.title: Topology Optimization of Machine Components

ME G621.description: Mechanics of turbulent flow; semi-empirical expressions; statistical concepts; stability theory;flow of non-Newtonian fluids; stationary and moving shock waves; Prandtl-Mayer expressions; two and three dimensional subsonic and supersonic flow; methods of characteristics; small perturbation theory and similarity rules.
ME G621.title: Fluid Dynamics

ME G622.description: Introduction to multiphase flow phenomena and classification: gas-liquid, liquid-solid, gas-solid, and threephase systems. Flow regimes, interfacial dynamics, and phase distribution in pipe and channel flows. Conservation equations for mass, momentum, and energy in multiphase systems. Models for homogeneous, separated, and drift-flux flow. Bubble dynamics, droplet formation, and particle motion. Heat and mass transfer in multiphase media. Applications to boiling, condensation, cavitation, fluidization, and spray systems. Flow regime maps, pressure drop correlations, and empirical modeling approaches. Numerical modeling using control volume and finite element frameworks. Laboratory sessions focused on visualization, measurements, and simulation of multiphase transport phenomena. Relevance to thermal systems, nuclear reactors, chemical processes, and energy systems.
ME G622.title: Multiphase Flow

ME G623.description: Comprehensive study of compressible flow and high-speed gas dynamics. Governing equations for inviscid and viscous compressible flows. One-dimensional flow with area change, friction, and heat addition. Shock waves: normal and oblique shocks, expansion waves, shock relations, and wave interactions. Quasionedimensional nozzle flow and performance analysis. Two-dimensional compressible flows, method of characteristics, and supersonic flow past bodies. Real gas effects, high-temperature flows, and non-equilibrium phenomena. Applications in propulsion, nozzles, diffusers, and high-speed aerodynamics. Introduction to numerical methods for solving hyperbolic systems of conservation laws. Laboratory and simulation components involve modeling of shock tube problems, nozzle flows, and compressible flow systems using inhouse computational tools. Emphasis on physical understanding, mathematical formulation, and practical relevance.
ME G623.title: Advanced Gas Dynamics

ME G624.description: Introduction to microfluidics and its relevance in thermal systems. Scaling laws, fluid dynamics, and heat transfer at the microscale. Theoretical foundations of microflows: continuum breakdown, slip flow, and rarefied gas effects. Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) for microfluidic thermal transport; concepts of discretization, meshing, and solver selection. Fabrication techniques for thermal microdevices: lithography, etching, and soft lithography. Design and analysis of microvalves, micropumps, and microchannels for thermal management. Integration of microheaters, microsensors, and micro heat exchangers. Microfluidics in energy systems: phase change cooling, thermal regulation in electronics, and compact heat recovery. Simulation and modeling using physics-based CAD tools. Laboratory components include design, simulation, and virtual testing of microfluidic thermal systems
ME G624.title: Microfluidics for Thermal Engineers

ME G625.description: Thermodynamic and fluid flow principles in food processing operations. Heat and mass transfer in food materials: conduction, convection, and radiation with phase change. Thermal processing methods: pasteurization, sterilization, drying, freezing, and evaporation. Fluid dynamics of food slurries, emulsions, and non-Newtonian fluids. Design and analysis of heat exchangers, dryers, evaporators, and refrigeration systems for food applications. Thermal degradation of nutrients and quality retention during processing. Transport properties of food materials and their temperature dependence. Computational modeling of thermal and fluid processes in food systems. Hygienic design, energy efficiency, and sustainability in thermal food equipment. Laboratory and simulation components include modeling of heat/moisture transfer, flow behavior of complex fluids, and process optimization for quality and safety.
ME G625.title: Thermo-fluidics of Food Processing

ME G626.description: Electrochemical Storage Systems Electrochemical energy conversion and storage fundamentals. Thermodynamics, kinetics, and mass transport in electrochemical systems. Battery technologies: lead-acid, nickel-based, lithiumion, sodium-ion, and flow batteries—design, performance metrics, degradation, and safety. Fuel cells: hydrogen, PEM, solid oxide, and alkaline types—working principles, materials, and system integration. Supercapacitors and hybrid systems. System modeling, charge–discharge behavior, efficiency, and thermal management. Applications in electric vehicles, grid storage, and portable electronics. Sustainability, recycling, and techno-economic analysis. Industry trends and emerging technologies in electrochemical storage systems. Associated laboratory.
ME G626.title: Batteries, Fuel Cells and Other

ME G627.description: AI applications in thermal energy systems from both renewable and non-renewable sources. Introduction to machine learning and data-driven modeling techniques relevant to energy conversion and thermal processes. AI-based forecasting of solar irradiance, wind profiles, and thermal loads. Optimization and control of solar thermal, biomass, geothermal, and waste-heat recovery systems. Intelligent diagnostics and efficiency enhancement in fossil-fuelbased thermal power plants. Predictive maintenance of boilers, turbines, and heat exchangers using machine learning. Energy management and optimization in combined heat and power (CHP), thermal storage, and hybrid energy systems. Thermal system modeling using AI-integrated simulation frameworks. Case studies and deployment of AI techniques using real-world datasets from renewable and conventional thermal energy sectors.
ME G627.title: Artificial Intelligence in Energy Systems

ME G628.description: Introduction to electric vehicle (EV) technology and architecture. Vehicle dynamics, drive cycles, and performance parameters. Electrical propulsion systems: motors (BLDC, PMSM, induction), motor controllers, and power electronics. Energy storage systems: battery types, characteristics, and battery management systems (BMS). Charging infrastructure, protocols, and power conversion. Regenerative braking, thermal management, and vehicle control strategies. Design considerations for range, efficiency, and reliability. Overview of hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), and fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs). Environmental impact and life cycle analysis of EV systems. Standards, policies, and market trends. Case studies on EV design, simulation, and integration challenges. Associated laboratory.
ME G628.title: Electric Vehicles

ME G629.description: Introduction to packaging and Thermal management, heat sinks, thermal interface materials, phase change materials, microchannels, immersion cooling, heat pipes, and thermoelectric solutions. Applications in avionics, automotive, aerospace, data centres, batteries, hydrogen and fuel cells, and mass transportation. Wafer fabrication, flip-chip bonding, multi-chip modules, system-on-chip (SoC), and specialized packages. Additional aspects in mechanical design, thermal modeling, reliability studies, and emerging trends in smart and adaptive thermal management. Associated lab and case studies to compliment the theoretical aspects.
ME G629.title: Thermal Management in Packaging

ME G630.description: Introduction to cryogenics, thermodynamics of cryogenic fluids, ultra-low temperature materials. Design of gas liquefaction and refrigeration systems, cryocoolers in space, quantum computing and medical technologies. Advanced gas separation for hydrogen production, cryogenic insulation for LNG storage. Superconductivity and its applications in energy storage, high-energy physics and superconducting magnets. Precision vacuum technology, instrumentation and control in cryogenic systems. Safety protocols in cryogenic operations. Industrial applications in aerospace, particle accelerators, and cryopreservation. Practical components include experimental studies of materials at cryogenic temperatures and their characterization, tests on superconductors for magnetic levitation and case studies
ME G630.title: Cryogenic Engineering and Applications

ME G631.description: Heat conduction with unsteady boundary conditions; recent advances in natural and forced convection; condensation and boiling phenomena; heat transfer in high speed flows; liquid metal heat transfer, radioactive metal heat-transfer between surfaces in absorbing media; complex problems involving simultaneous conduction, convection and radiation.
ME G631.title: Advanced Heat Transfer

ME G632.description: Principles and practices of energy auditing in industrial, commercial, and residential sectors. Energy flow analysis, benchmarking, and energy performance assessment. Instruments and techniques for energy auditing: power analyzers, thermography, flow meters, and data loggers. Analysis of thermal systems: boilers, furnaces, heat exchangers, HVAC systems, and thermal utilities. Electrical system analysis: motors, drives, lighting, and power quality. Energy management strategies: demand-side management, load scheduling, peak load control, and power factor improvement. Economic analysis: life cycle costing, payback, net present value, and cost– benefit analysis. Standards and policies: ISO 50001, energy conservation building code (ECBC), and government regulations. Case studies of successful energy conservation projects. Practical component includes field audits, report preparation, and simulation-based energy analysis of thermal and electrical systems.
ME G632.title: Energy Auditing and Management

ME G633.description: Fundamentals of wind energy and atmospheric dynamics. Wind characteristics, statistical analysis of wind data, and site assessment. Aerodynamics of wind turbines: blade element theory, momentum theory, and rotor design principles. Types of wind turbines: horizontal and vertical axis, operational regimes, and control strategies. Structural dynamics, loads, and fatigue analysis. Electrical aspects: generators, power electronics, and grid integration. System modeling: wind resource estimation, turbine performance, and farm-level energy prediction using analytical and numerical methods. Economic evaluation: cost of energy, lifecycle analysis, and feasibility studies. Laboratory and simulation components include wind data analysis, turbine modeling, and software-based performance prediction. Standards, certification procedures, environmental impacts, and policy frameworks for wind energy deployment.
ME G633.title: Wind Energy Systems Modelling and Analysis

ME G634.description: Systems Overview of bioenergy resources: biomass classification, availability, and characterization. Thermochemical and biochemical conversion processes: combustion, gasification, pyrolysis, anaerobic digestion, and fermentation. Modeling of biomass feedstock supply chains, conversion processes, and product utilization. Energy and mass balance calculations for bioenergy systems. Reactor models and kinetics of biomass conversion. Simulation of biogas, bioethanol, biodiesel, and syngas production systems. System integration with thermal and power generation applications. Technoeconomic analysis, environmental impact, and lifecycle assessment. Laboratory and simulation components include modeling of bioenergy pathways using simulation tools and case studies. Applications in rural energy, industrial heat, and grid-connected bioenergy systems. National policies, incentives, and sustainability standards for bioenergy deployment
ME G634.title: Modelling and Simulation of Bioenergy

ME G635.description: and Heat Transfer Fundamentals of finite element methods (FEM) for solving fluid flow and heat transfer problems. Governing equations: conservation of mass, momentum (Navier–Stokes), and energy. Weak formulation, weighted residual methods, and Galerkin approach. Discretization techniques, element types, shape functions, and numerical integration. FEM applications in steady and unsteady heat conduction, convection, and radiation problems. Formulation and solution strategies for incompressible and compressible flows. Coupled thermofluid analysis and boundary condition implementation. Introduction to turbulence modeling and stability analysis. Hands-on modeling and simulation assignments using generalpurpose computational frameworks. Applications to thermal systems, energy devices, and flow domains. Emphasis on accuracy, convergence, mesh independence, and physical validation of results.
ME G635.title: Finite Element Modelling of Fluid Flows

ME G636.description: Systems Comprehensive study of thermal and hybrid power generation technologies with an emphasis on modern practices and sustainability. In-depth analysis of steam, gas turbine, combined cycle, and nuclear power plants, along with the integration of renewable energy sources and thermal storage. Thermodynamic modeling of Rankine, Brayton, and regenerative cycles incorporating reheat, regeneration, and intercooling techniques. Detailed exploration of key components including boilers, combustion chambers, turbines, condensers, cooling systems, and heat recovery units. Focus on performance optimization, part-load operation, and exergy analysis. Examination of environmental control measures such as NOₓ/SOₓ mitigation, CO₂ capture, and waste heat recovery. Economic assessment using levelized cost of electricity, tariff structures, and operational efficiency metrics. Emphasis on hybrid configurations and the role of modeling tools for simulation and analysis.
ME G636.title: Thermal and Hybrid Power Generation

ME G637.description: Introduction and Origin of Turbulence; Correlation Functions, Kolmogorov Hypothesis and Probability Density Function; Reynolds Averaged Navier-Stokes Equations and Classical Idealization of Turbulent Flows; Vorticity Dynamics; Dynamics of Turbulent Kinetic Energy and Important Scaling Relations; Wall Bounded Flows and Free Shear Flows; Spectral Dynamics; Mathematical Modeling of Turbulent Flows; Introduction to experimental methods.
ME G637.title: Turbulent Flows

ME G638.description: Equations of motion in rotating coordinate frames, Cartesian approximations, Density stratified flows and internal gravity waves, Taylor-Proudman theorem, Ekman layer, single and multiple layered shallow-water systems, Geostrophic adjustment and Thermal-wind balance, Potential vorticity, Poincare, Kelvin and Rossby waves, Kelvin-Helmholtz instability, Baroclinic instability, Wavemean theory, 2D turbulence, chaotic advection in Stratosphere, Laplace tidal equations, Internal tides in deep oceans, tsunami waves.
ME G638.title: Geophysical Fluid Dynamics

ME G639.description: Introduction: Continuity, momentum and energy equations in Cartesian and cylindrical coordinates. Basics of buoyancy driven flows. Dimensionless numbers. Mixing and transport processes in environmental fluid systems. Advective and diffusive mixing. Turbulence and stratification. Boussinesq and hydrostatic approximations; Vertical flows: Vorticity dynamics. MTT model. Turbulent plumes. Filling box flows; Horizontal flows: Shallow water approximation. Gravity currents. Surface waves; Flow through Porous Media: Darcy’s law. Dispersion. Contaminant transport. Thermal and Haline convection. Gravity currents. Capillary effects; Introduction to instabilities: Kelvin-Helmholtz Instability. Rayleigh-Taylor instability. Saffman-Taylor instability
ME G639.title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics

ME G640.description: Fundamentals of rocket propulsion systems and their application in space missions. Thermodynamics and gas dynamics of propulsion cycles. Classification of propulsion systems: chemical, electric, and advanced propulsion methods. Solid, liquid, and hybrid rocket engines: design principles, performance analysis, combustion processes, and propellant characteristics. Thrust generation, nozzle design, specific impulse, and staging. Orbital mechanics and mission planning basics. Introduction to electric propulsion: ion thrusters, Halleffect thrusters, and plasma-based systems. Heat transfer, cooling techniques, and structural considerations in propulsion systems. Laboratory and simulation sessions on propulsion system modeling, thrust chamber analysis, and trajectory estimation. Emphasis on performance evaluation, system integration, and recent advancements in launch and in-space propulsion technologies.
ME G640.title: Rocket and Space Craft Propulsion

ME G641.description: Basic equations of theory of elasticity; elementary elasticity problems in two and three dimensions; theories of plastic flow; problems in plastic flow of ideally plastic and strain hardening materials; theory of metal forming processes.
ME G641.title: Theory of Elasticity and Plasticity

ME G642.description: Engineering Introduction: generalized measurement system, static calibration, calibration, random errors, uncertainty analysis, dynamic characteristics. Zero, first and second order measurement systems. Temperature measurement: Introduction to temperature measurement. Thermocouples: laws governing their use; Static and Dynamic characteristics. Other measurement techniques. Pressure measurement: Manometers, elastic transducers, static and dynamic characteristics. Other devices for measurement. Flow measurement: obstruction meters, variable area meters, velocity measurement. Strain measurement: electrical type strain gauges, metallic resistance strain gauge, selection and installation of strain gages, circuitry for strain measurement, temperature compensation, calibration, semi-conductor strain gauges, stress analysis methods Force and torque measurement: standards, elastic transducers, strain gage load cells, hydraulic and pneumatic systems, torque measurement, combined force and moment measurement. Measurement of motion: LVDT, general theory of seismic instruments, vibrometers and accelerometers, piezoelectric accelerometers and vibrometers-circuitry and calibration, exciter systems, vibration test methods. Signal conditioning: Operational amplifiers, filters. Associated laboratory with experiments on all the above measurements Microelectronics
ME G642.title: Experimental Techniques in Thermal

MEL G512.description: Course Content: Elemental and Compound Semiconductors, Optical Physics and Processes in Semiconductors, Semiconductor Theory, p-n Junction, Light Emitting Diodes (LEDs), Semiconductor LASERs, p-i-n Diode, Avalanche Photodiode (APD), Photoconductors, Image Sensors, Solar Cells, Optical Waveguides, Resonators, Filters, Couplers, Multiplexers, WDM Devices, Gratings, Amplifiers, Modulation Techniques for optical signals, Optical Modulators and Switches, Guided and Unguided System Design and Applications, Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs), Emerging trends in optoelectronic devices and circuits. Laboratory Experiments: Characterization of LEDs and laser diodes, Measurement of photodetector characteristics, Design and implementation of simple optoelectronic circuits, Experiments with optical modulation and switching.
MEL G512.title: Optoelectronic Devices, Circuits and Sys- tems

MEL G514.description: Memory Systems for Modern Processors: Architecture, Circuits, and Technology, Optimization of memory systems in modern computing architectures, covering their hierarchical organization, circuit innovations, and emerging technologies. Students will study the role of DRAM, SRAM, eDRAM, Flash, and CAM architectures in processors, GPUs, and embedded cores, along with techniques to improve latency, bandwidth, and power efficiency, pipelining, memory banking, cache optimizations, and multi-core integration while addressing challenges in next-generation nonvolatile and 3D-stacked memory technologies.
MEL G514.title: Nanoelectronic Memories and Technology

MEL G521.description: Introduction to memory devices in SRAM, DRAM and 3DNAND Flash, circuit and device considerations, device fabrication techniques and scaling avenues, memory array addressing, readout circuits, device characterization, reliability characterization. Nonvolatile memory cell structures like (1T-1C 6T, 4T, 1T-1R, 0T- 1R, 1S-1R, floating gate FLASH, SONOS, NROM), and memory organization (open bit-line, folded bit-line, NAND, NOR, cross-point etc.), new memory devices and concepts including (e.g. magnetic tunnel junction memory (MRAM, SST-RAM), ferroelectric memory (FRAM), phase change memory (PCM), metal oxide resistive switching memory (RRAM), nano conductive bridge memory (CBRAM).
MEL G521.title: Novel Memory Concepts and Technology

MEL G522.description: CMOS technology scaling and its implications, process variabilities, layout dependent performance variation and reliability, Fin- FETs based designs compact modelling, simulation, standard cells and memory creation, FDSOI technology for digital and analog design, DSP enabled frequency synthesizers, fractional and DPLL architectures, digitally controlled oscillators, loop filters, adaptive spur cancellation in PLLs, linearity calibration of SAR ADC, CMOS self-healing techniques for calibration and optimization, analog assisted digital design in SoCs.
MEL G522.title: Digitally Assisted Analog Circuits

MEL G523.description: Circuits PLLs basic model and analysis, discrete and integrated techniques Phase and Frequency Synthesis, phase noise and spurs, phase detectors, frequency dividers, voltage-controlled oscillators, fractional PLL, direct digital synthesis, DPLL, ADPLL, Frequency acquisition, Clock multipliers, Analog phase error detectors, charge pump PLL design and challenges, ring oscillators, phase and jitter noise analysis, clock and data recovery circuits.
MEL G523.title: Phase and Frequency Synthesis of Analog

MEL G528.description: Introduction to MOS Physics, Static NMOS/CMOS inverter: Voltage Transfer Characteristics, CMOS Process Technology, Layout and Design Rules, Scaling of MOS Devices, CMOS Combinational and Sequential Logic Circuit, Static and Dynamic CMOS Logic Design, Power Dissipation in CMOS Circuits, Logical Effort, and Clocking Strategies. Introduction to Finfet based Circuit Design, ALU, Barrel shifter, Memory sub system.
MEL G528.title: Digital VLSI Design

MEL G532.description: Introduction to hardware security and trust, Finite Fields, AES Hardware, S-Box, Cryptography, Algorithm to Hardware, ECC, Basics of VLSI Design and Test, Security Based on PUFs and TRNGs, Machine Learning of PUFs, Hardware Metering, Watermarking of HW IPs, Physical Attacks, Fault Injection Attacks, Hardware Trojans: Detection and Prevention, Counterfeit Detection and Avoidance, Side Channel Attacks and Countermeasures, FPGA security measures, Advanced Micro-architectural attacks, Hardware monitoring for malwares using Hardware Performance Counters.
MEL G532.title: Hardware Security

MEL G533.description: Processor test, Memory build in self-test (MBIST), Logic BIST, Memory redundancy, Memory repair, SOC Testing (3D integration, Test Access Mechanism (TAM), IDDQ testing, and Static DAC/ADC testing) Structured scan techniques standardized by the IEEE: IEEE-1149.1 (JTAG), IEEE-1149.x, IEEE-1500, IEEE- 1687 IJTAG, Analog and Mixed Signal Test, Power issues during test, Low power test pattern generation, Power aware system level test planning, Test Strategies for: Multi-voltage Designs/Gated Clock Designs/Power management structures.
MEL G533.title: SOC Test and Power Aware Testing

MEL G541.description: Formal verification trend in industry and challenges, Modelling sequential and parallel systems, CTL and LTL temporal logics, deadlock and liveness issues; fairness; model checking techniques, automata-based approaches and bounded model checking with SAT solvers, BDD data-structure, SMT solvers, Assertionbased software verification, Completeness thresholds and k-induction Symbolic execution Craig interpolation, Software model checking, pattern based detection of concurrency bugs, introduction to commercial formal verification tools.
MEL G541.title: Hardware and Software Formal Verification

MEL G611.description: Material properties; crystal growth and doping; diffusion; oxidation; epitaxy; ion implantation; deposition of films using CVD, LPCVD and sputtering techniques; wet and dry etching and cleaning; lithographic process; device and circuit fabrication; process modeling and simulation.
MEL G611.title: IC Fabrication Technology

MEL G612.description: General architectural features of 8/16/32 bit microprocessors, programmers model of 8086, assembly language programming, hardware design around 8086, bus based systems design, system design around IBM PC, design of real-time systems, ASIC's development tools.
MEL G612.title: Integrated Electronics Systems Design

MEL G621.description: Introduction to NMOS and CMOS circuits; NMOS and CMOS processing technology; CMOS circuits and logic design; circuit characterization and performance estimation; structured design and testing; symbolic layout systems; CMOS subsystem design; system case studies.
MEL G621.title: VLSI Design

MEL G622.description: Fundamentals and definitions; Perceptrons, backpropagation and counterpropagation Networks; Statistical methods for network training; Hopfield nets; Associative memories; Optical neural networks; Applications of neural networks in speech processing, computer networks and visual processing.
MEL G622.title: Introduction to Artificial Neural Networks

MEL G623.description: Design of clocked VLSI systems, Timing issues, Synchronous register/latch-based systems, Asynchronous systems, handshake protocols, signaling-current mode/ voltage mode, Clock signals distribution and clock generation, low power clock drivers, I/O drivers, Digital phase locked loop, delay locked loop, Synchronizer design and meta-stability issues in multi-clock domain, Wire design models in nanometer regionlumped, distributed, transmission line, termination, transmitter/ receiver drivers, Low power VLSI Circuits-Adiabatic logic circuits, Low Vdd/ Low Vt design. Stacked CMOS, Low power SRAM, Noise in digital systems, Power supply distribution, Introduction to Deep submicron device behavior and nanometer devices, Design implementations of architectural functional blocks (high-speed arithmetic circuits) using ASIC technology and FPGA technology.
MEL G623.title: Advanced VLSI Design

MEL G624.description: Advanced VLSI processor architectures, their implementation strategies (microarchitectures) and associated memory hierarchies and their micro-architectures for high performance system design. Various techniques utilized to leverage parallelism at hardware, application and compiler levels. Concept of (beyond instruction-level parallelism) data-level parallelism, thread-level parallelism and task level parallelism to architect and implement different processing cores e.g.: Vector Processors, SIMD processors and Multimedia processors, Graphical Processing Units (GPU) and General Purpose Graphical Processing Units (GPGPU), Multi-core processors, Introduction to Network on chips (NOC), Domain Specific Processors and Memory hierarchy organizations for the above processors. Emerging research directions in VLSI processor design and system architectures.
MEL G624.title: Advanced VLSI Architectures

MEL G625.description: Mixed signal blocks design issues, Design of high-resolution, high-speed Comparators, Data Converters Architectures, Oscillators, Frequency Synthesizers, Phase Locked Loop, Integrated Voltage Regulators, Power Management Circuits, CMOS multipliers, dividers, and modulators, Filters-active/ passive/ switched capacitor, Signal Conditioning and sensor associated circuits, Energy Harvesting Circuits, Issues in Analog Testing and Analog layouts, Noise issues.
MEL G625.title: Advanced Analog and Mixed Signal Design

MEL G626.description: Fault models and types; automated test generation for combinational logic; test generation for sequential logic; need for adding testability logic; design for testability; Adhoc DFT methods; structured DFT; test generation for delay fault; issues in analog circuit testing and testability.
MEL G626.title: VLSI Test and Testability

MEL G627.description: Historical perspective; Processing overview; Crystallography of semiconductors; Defects in semiconductors; Clean room; Wafergrowth; cleaning; oxidation; epitaxy; wet and dry etching; lithographic process; diffusion; ion implantation; deposition of films using CVD, and PVD techniques; device and circuit fabrication; Process Integration: Passive components, Bipolar Technology and MOSFET Technology, Fabrication of advanced VLSI devices; System on chip; Future trends and Challenges: Laboratory components: Simulation of key fabrication processes using CAD tools; Demonstration of basic fab line processes; Fabrication and testing of electronic devices.
MEL G627.title: VLSI Fabrication Technology

MEL G631.description: Physics and properties of semiconductor - a review; Semiconductor transport model, modeling of metal-semiconductor junctions, pn homojunction and heterjunctions, bipolar transistor, JFET, MESFET, HEMT and; MOS capacitor, modeling of MOSFET, scaling issues, and recent trends in advanced MOSFETs Laboratory components: Modeling and simulation of silicon based devices with TCAD software. I-V, C-V measurement of MS and MOS junctions.
MEL G631.title: Physics and Modelling of Microelectronic Devices

MEL G632.description: Basic Analog IC Design Issues, MOS Switch--Charge Injection, Current and Voltage Biasing and Reference Generation Circuits, Design, and Analysis of Single Stage Amplifiers, Differential Amplifiers, Common Mode Feedback Circuit, Replica Bias, Operational Amplifiers, and Operational Trans-conductance Amplifier Design, Frequency Compensation, Noise- Analysis and Estimation in Amplifiers, Introduction to Low Power OPAMP, OPAMP/ OTA design in Subthreshold Operation region, Introduction to Current Mode Analog Circuit Design, Analog Layouts.
MEL G632.title: Analog IC Design

MEL G633.description: Functions and applications of D/A and A/D converters, ideal DACs and ADCs: operation, specifications, metrics., converter non-idealities, sampling, noise, nonidealities and distortion, gate boosted switches, charge injection, sample and hold characterization, delta sigma modulation, stability analysis, linearized analysis, NTF designs and criteria, antialiasing, CTDM, ELD, clock jitter, integrator design, flash ADC, auto zeroing techniques, segmented DACs, calibration and randomization, dynamic element matching.
